baseline.functionsExecutionToday: support/functions-host.cjs loads the consumer's firebase-tools 15.22.0 FunctionsEmulator and ExtensionsEmulator; Rust owns registration, event envelopes, delivery, Pub/Sub, scheduling and readiness

ownership.discoveryWireManifest: firebase-functions-sdk-7.2.5-source (lib/runtime/manifest.js stackToWire, served as JSON at /__/functions.yaml when FUNCTIONS_CONTROL_API=true)

oracles.classificationRule: match the official emulator; where Fireside deliberately differs (it must not fail startup on an upstream-ignored export, one worker per codebase instead of one per trigger, no Google Analytics call per invocation) the difference is recorded in the fixture invariants and asserted by the replay; no divergence is adopted silently and no fixture is edited after freezing

production.usedFor: nothing unless H1 finds an emulator behaviour the SDK documents as different in production; every such case is listed here before implementation

supportedTriggerMatrix.policy: every row is captured in H1 and replayed in H2; anything outside the matrix is an ignored export with a recorded reason, never a silent drop and never a startup failure
v2: onCustomEventPublished (only if H1 shows the official emulator delivers Extensions events)
ignoredWithReason: taskQueueTrigger (extension resources: dropped by firebase-tools 15.22.0 triggerHelper; user functions: Tasks emulator delivery stays unimplemented)
Realtime Database, Remote Config, Test Lab, Crashlytics, Analytics, Firebase Alerts and Eventarc channel events outside the Extensions case
onCall genkitAction and Data Connect GraphQL triggers

workerModel.policy: one Node worker per codebase (user codebase or extension instance), started at readiness, restarted on crash and on source reload; FUNCTION_TARGET, FUNCTION_SIGNATURE_TYPE and K_SERVICE are set synchronously before each invocation; the official emulator starts one worker per trigger lazily
workerModel.recordedIn: fixture invariants: handlers observe the same per-invocation environment on both engines; process identity is not part of the contract

discovery.policy: spawn the codebase's own node_modules/.bin/firebase-functions with FUNCTIONS_CONTROL_API=true and read /__/functions.yaml (JSON body), then /__/quitquitquit; a static functions.yaml in the source directory takes precedence as in firebase-tools; the manifest is the SDK's stackToWire v1alpha1 contract

extensionsRegistry.policy: reuse the Firebase CLI's stored account (configstore) refresh token when present, accept FIREBASE_TOKEN, and add `fireside ext:vendor` offline mode; an own OAuth login flow is not in this phase
extensionsRegistry.cacheDirectory: FIREBASE_EXTENSIONS_CACHE_PATH or ~/.cache/firebase/extensions/<publisher>/<name>@<version>, shared with firebase-tools so nothing is downloaded twice
extensionsRegistry.vendoredSources: <project>/extensions/.sources/<publisher>/<name>@<version> (or the configured directory) preferred over the cache; a fully vendored project starts with no network and no token

taskQueueTrigger.policy: extension resources with taskQueueTrigger are admitted without delivery and reported as ignored with reason `firebase-tools 15.22.0 drops taskQueueTrigger from emulated extension definitions`, so the Twodart extensions gate keeps its 2 ignored records

eventarc.policy: registration routes stay; H1 measured that the official Eventarc emulator delivers Extensions custom events published through the Admin SDK channel to user onCustomEventPublished handlers (extensions-triggers/publish-listened), so H2 adds delivery for Eventarc channel events
eventarc.settled: delivered by the official emulator; Fireside implements channel event delivery

credentialIsolation.policy: workers never receive the developer's ADC or CLI credentials; GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is unset in worker environments and the registry token is used by the Rust parent only

capture.handlerObservation: every handler appends {invocation, env subset, request shape or event envelope, auth context} to a JSONL file the harness reads back; the fixture records the observation next to the HTTP step that caused it

firebaseToolsSurfacesToRemove.what: FUNCTIONS_HOST_SOURCE include_str!, SuiteConfig.firebase_tools_root, preflight row ("firebase-tools", ...), spawn_functions_host --firebase-tools-root
doc comments naming the pinned firebase-tools host (behaviour unchanged)
every statement that firebase-tools is required by the Fireside path

emulatorReplay.test: crates/functions-runtime replay of conformance/fixtures/functions-runtime-v1 over HTTP against a started runtime

existingFixturesUnchanged.policy: their contracts are the suite's, not the host's; they keep passing without edits

noFirebaseTools.ciStep: Verify suite start without firebase-tools in node_modules

extensions.twodartExtensionsGate: bun test:fireside-extensions passes on the packed candidate with 26 definitions, 24 admitted, 2 ignored with reasons
extensions.offlineStart: a project with every extension vendored starts with the network blocked and no CLI token

performance.profile: Hetzner paired acceptance function lane and suite readiness

acceptance.exactCandidateCi: all jobs including the new no-firebase-tools step

h1.reRecordedBecause: the replay harness settled its digest rules (served extension specs are parameter-substituted; registry objects carry volatile install counts) after the first capture; same programs, same counts. Frozen text then normalized for portability without a recapture: macOS /private real-path prefix folded into {{projectDir}}, the SDK's node_modules directory as {{nodeModules}}, Express error-page stack frames as {{stack}}

profiles.twodart-refs: 10/10 offline from the shared cache with registry sidecars (FIRESIDE_OFFLINE=1)
